author: Forrest Swan III

projects.name: license-exam-prep
projects.title: License Exam Prep
projects.tagline: Offline Windows desktop app for Florida insurance license practice exams across six license tracks.

detail.problem: Agents studying for Florida license exams had no practice tool that ran on the locked-down Allstate-managed workstations (no add-ins, no macros, no cloud installs).
detail.solution: A standalone one-file `.exe` (PyWebView + SQLite + ReportLab) with full-length timed exams that follow the official Pearson VUE Florida content outlines (effective 2026-01-01), a projected-score gauge, per-domain mastery, and branded PDF reports.
highlights: 1,467 outline-mapped practice questions (500 hand-written master items) across 2-20, 20-44, 4-40, 2-15, 2-14 and 2-40 tracks
Blueprints are data (`data/blueprints/blueprints.json`, weights validated at startup) — no code change to update an outline
Optional AI narrative report via the Anthropic API (key DPAPI-encrypted) with a deterministic offline fallback
17 automated tests pass (zero-dependency runner, verified 2026-09-22)
detail.diagram:
flowchart LR UI[Web UI
index.html + app.js] -- js_api --> API[api.py] API --> ASM[assembler.py
blueprint-weighted sampling] ASM --> BANK[(data/banks/*.json)] ASM --> BP[(blueprints.json)] API --> DB[(SQLite attempts)] DB --> PROJ[projection.py
recency-weighted mastery] API --> RPT[reports_ai.py / reports_pdf.py] RPT -->|optional| ANT[Anthropic API] RPT --> PDF[PDF report]
notes: Question content is original training material written to the public content outlines; it is not sourced from secured exam items.
Logo files in `web/assets/` are neutral placeholders.

projects.name: training-program
projects.title: Agency Training Program
projects.tagline: Internal training platform: video modules, randomized question banks, remediation gates and automatic score emails.

detail.problem: Staff training lived in scattered decks and videos with no quiz tracking and no way for managers to see results.
detail.solution: A desktop app where content is data: each module (video, slides, chapters, question bank, Core Process document) lives in `content/` next to the exe and is added through a built-in import wizard — no code change or rebuild.
highlights: Quiz engine v2: per-attempt draws round-robin across sections with shuffled questions and options
Fail ⇒ remediation gate: sections tied to missed questions must be rewatched (server-enforced) before a retake
Scores emailed to the right manager via Outlook COM automation (works where the M365 tenant blocks SMTP AUTH); failed sends queue in SQLite and retry
Documents open in an in-app PDF.js viewer; topbar search across narration, slides, documents and links
39 automated tests pass (verified 2026-09-22)
detail.diagram:
flowchart LR W[Import wizard] -->|PPTX→PNG via PowerPoint COM
quiz draft via Claude API| C[(content/module folders)] C --> M[modules.py
schema validation] M --> UI[Web UI + search] UI --> Q[scoring.py
bank draw + remediation] Q --> DB[(SQLite)] Q --> P[reports_pdf.py] P --> E[emailer.py
Outlook COM / SMTP + retry queue] UI --> S[server.py
localhost Range server for video seek]
notes: `content/` (training videos and decks) and `config/roster.json` are not in the repo; the roster in `koi_training/roster.py` is fictional.
`web-portal/` holds a later browser-based variant (single HTML page + PHP roster API) and its Playwright end-to-end test.

projects.name: filegate
projects.title: FileGate — Naming Compliance Auditor + AI Intake
projects.tagline: Scans the agency file share against the data policy, and files staff uploads automatically with AI field extraction. Completed and in production.

detail.problem: Client files on the shared NAS drifted from the agency naming and folder policy, and nobody could see who owned the violations.
detail.solution: A Windows desktop/headless auditor that encodes the data policy as a JSON ruleset, resolves the NTFS owner of every item, locks a baseline compliance score per employee, and applies reversible in-place renames. FileGate Intake adds a Google Apps Script upload page that stages files in Drive for an on-prem agent to rename and file.
highlights: Policy is data (`rulesets/data_policy_v1.6.json`); underivable names go to a Pending-Review proposal instead of being guessed
Measured a VPN bottleneck (~178 → ~7 items/s over the tunnel), added a LAN gate, incremental commits and explicit failure states, then moved the weekly scan to an always-on office PC
Live scan: 67,240 items in 24 minutes with 0 errors (2026-09-22)
Intake: staff drop a file; an on-site agent extracts client, document type and address with the Claude API, renames to policy and files it, and parks anything it can't match for human review
62 automated tests pass; a 388,000-row database migration verified before go-live
Staff training shipped 2026-09-24: 33-slide deck, two narrated videos, a 24-question quiz and two SOPs
notes: Completed: in production since 2026-09-23. Compliance-rate improvement will be published once rename cycles begin.

projects.name: uw-triage
projects.title: UW Triage Engine + Board
projects.tagline: Turns carrier underwriting notices into tracked work items with an AI triage engine, a web board, and two-way Slack.

detail.problem: Underwriting notices arrived by email and got lost; there was no single list of what was due, who owned it, or what was past due.
detail.solution: An Apps Script engine reads the notices mailbox, extracts structured fields with the Claude API, and writes items to a Sheet; a web-app board lets agents work items, with Slack DMs, a daily digest, and command parsing from Slack threads.
highlights: Board shipped through v2.10.5 (web-app version 62, 2026-09-22); engine v1.4 with legacy-source backfill
Two-way Slack by polling (Apps Script cannot read Slack signing headers), all writes through one write path
Single "Past Due" flag in days; daily digest at or after 5 PM ET
Board regression suites recorded 0 failures at v2.10 (per the deploy record)

projects.name: audit-system
projects.title: Audit & Compliance Scoring System
projects.tagline: Self-hosted QC audit system: random policy sampling, rubric scoring, UW issue tracking and dashboards on a NAS.

detail.problem: Policy file quality was checked ad hoc with no sampling method, no rubric, and no record of findings.
detail.solution: A free-tier, self-hosted stack on the office NAS (Docker via Container Station): seeded stratified sampling, a versioned YAML rubric, JotForm human-in-the-loop checklists feeding n8n, findings in Postgres, and Metabase dashboards.
highlights: Pure, unit-tested scoring and sampling functions
Migrations 000–003 including a unified `uw_issue` table for scheduled audits and reactive intake
Designed around a hard constraint: the carrier portal allows no automation, so ~30–40% of checks stay human-in-the-loop

projects.name: apps-script-toolkit
projects.title: Apps Script Toolkit
projects.tagline: Google Apps Script tools: KPI tracker automation, monthly quiz form generator, spend tracker import, and a team quick-launch hub.

detail.problem: Operations reporting and staff tools were manual spreadsheets and bookmarks, and the M365 environment blocked macros and add-ins.
detail.solution: Small, focused Apps Script projects that run in the consumer Google environment the agency is allowed to automate.
highlights: `kpi-tracker/` — computes business-hours SLA columns (Mon–Fri 8a–6p) as values, weekly roster row generation, 10-minute refresh trigger
`monthly-quiz/` — builds five auto-graded Google Forms with shuffled choices and per-item feedback
`spend-tracker/` — CSV import dialog, formula repair and menu for a multi-source spend workbook
`quick-launch-hub/` — full-width web-app hub embedded in the team site (v1.2, 2026-09-22)

projects.name: training-video-pipeline
projects.title: Narrated Training Video Pipeline
projects.tagline: Turns slide decks and narration scripts into narrated MP4 training videos plus HTML players with time-synced clickable links.

detail.problem: Slide-deck trainings were not self-serve, and MP4 files cannot carry clickable links.
detail.solution: A script pipeline: slides rendered to PNG, narration synthesized per slide with edge-tts, segments assembled with ffmpeg, and an HTML player that overlays time-synced link hotspots on the video.
highlights: Six videos shipped 2026-07-14 to 2026-07-15 (PDFelement, reMarkable 2, RoboForm trainings and their Core Process videos)
Player hotspots positioned from python-pptx shape bounding boxes
Pronunciation transforms for acronyms and product names; segments validated with ffprobe before concat
detail.diagram:
flowchart LR PPTX[Deck] --> PNG[LibreOffice → pdftoppm
slide PNGs] SCR[docs/narration-*.md] --> SEG[src/segments_tts.json] SEG --> TTS[src/tts_generate.py
edge-tts per segment] PNG --> FF[ffmpeg segment encode] TTS --> FF FF --> MP4[Video MP4] MP4 --> PL[players/player-*.html
time-synced link overlays]

projects.name: design-system
projects.title: Design System
projects.tagline: Brand tokens (CSS variables, JS theme, Tailwind config) and ten React components for consistent agency web work.

detail.problem: Web pages and generated artifacts drifted from the agency brand.
detail.solution: One source of truth: `src/tokens.css`, mirrored in `src/theme.js` and `tailwind.config.js`, consumed by a small React component library and documented in `design-system.md`.
highlights: Palette, type scale, spacing, radius and elevation tokens with WCAG AA usage rules
10 components (Badge, Button, Card, Footer, Hero, Input, NavBar, QuoteCTA, ServiceTile, Testimonial), barrel-exported from src/components/index.js
detail.diagram:
flowchart LR
  T[src/tokens.css] --> J[src/theme.js]
  T --> TW[tailwind.config.js]
  T --> C[src/components/*.jsx]
  C --> P[preview.html]
notes: Brand logo URLs were replaced with a placeholder.

projects.name: sdr-talk-path
projects.title: SDR Talk Path Companion
projects.tagline: Interactive call-script companion for sales development reps, embedded in WordPress/Elementor.

detail.problem: New SDRs needed consistent, situation-specific call paths for cross-sell conversations.
detail.solution: A self-contained JS/HTML widget with talk paths per client situation (e.g. auto-only, home-only, renter), keyword search and routing hints, delivered as an Elementor widget and a WPCode snippet.
highlights: Three delivery formats: Elementor embed (v1.1), Elementor widget (v1.2), WPCode JS snippet (v1.2)
detail.diagram:
flowchart LR DATA[Talk-path data in JS] --> UI[Widget UI
search + steps] UI --> WP[WordPress page via Elementor or WPCode]
notes: Staff routing names in the data are fictional.

projects.name: pfsense-wireguard-vpn
projects.title: Secure Remote Access — pfSense Firewall + WireGuard VPN
projects.tagline: Designed, deployed and manage the agency firewall and staff VPN so remote staff reach office systems as if at their desks.

detail.problem: Remote and hybrid staff needed the office file server and printers, but the agency had no firewall-managed VPN and staff laptops have no admin rights.
detail.solution: A Netgate 2100 running pfSense as the office firewall, with WireGuard as the single staff VPN, rolled out so non-admin users can switch the tunnel on and off themselves.
highlights: Deployed and brought the VPN live in December 2025; 20+ remote and in-office users onboarded
Non-admin rollout: WireGuard installed as a Windows service with a limited network-operator role (January 2026)
VPN access revocation built into employee offboarding
Firewall management locked down to an admin workstation
Diagnosed a server-side routing/NAT gap blocking remote access to office systems and restored access (August 2026)
Measured VPN latency against file-share operations; the data moved bulk scans onto the office LAN
notes: Network specifics (addresses, interfaces, peers) are intentionally omitted.

projects.name: qnap-nas
projects.title: Agency File Server — QNAP NAS as System of Record
projects.tagline: Researched, proposed, installed and manage the NAS that became the single source of truth for client files.

detail.problem: Client files were scattered across personal drives and laptops, creating data-liability and E&O exposure and making files hard to find.
detail.solution: A QNAP TVS-h674 on QuTS hero (ZFS) with per-employee accounts, a folder-permission model and least-privilege service accounts for automation; reachable remotely over the WireGuard VPN.
highlights: Compared three NAS platforms at different price points and pitched the owners (July 2025)
Wrote the FY2026 Technology Budget Proposal including the NAS line (October 2025)
Ordered, built and brought the system live in-office (November–December 2025)
Least-privilege, file-sharing-only service account for automation
Hosts the staff Training Program web edition over LAN and VPN
About 67,000 client-file items under a weekly naming-compliance scan (see FileGate)
notes: Share names, addresses and accounts are intentionally omitted.

projects.name: remote-print-server
projects.title: Remote Printing Service
projects.tagline: An always-on office print server so staff can print to office printers from anywhere over the VPN.

detail.problem: Staff could only print while physically in the office.
detail.solution: A dedicated always-on office print server sharing the office printers, reachable over the VPN, with a one-page staff setup guide.
highlights: Live for the shared office printers since August 28, 2026
Staff setup guide v1.1: connect VPN, open the print server, add a printer
Jobs sent while the VPN is off queue and release on reconnect
notes: In progress: remaining printers being brought onto the service.

projects.name: it-department
projects.title: Establishing the Agency IT Department
projects.tagline: Built the agency IT function from scratch: budget, purchasing, vendor management, support intake and device lifecycle.

detail.problem: The agency had no IT function; purchasing, vendors, support and equipment were handled ad hoc.
detail.solution: A dedicated IT function with a technology budget, a vendor and systems ledger, a tiered support model and a managed device lifecycle.
highlights: Promoted to Technical Solutions Manager (August 2025), full-time from November 2025, then Agency Operations & Systems Manager (April 2026)
Authored the FY2026 Technology Department Budget
Launched equipment-request intake with weekly ordering (November 2025)
Support model: Windows 11 support chatbot first line, then an IT request form with a 1-business-day response
Systems ledger of 81 tools; System Administrator on 41
Onboarding/offboarding, device imaging and a wipe/recycle/donation pipeline

projects.name: asset-inventory
projects.title: Asset Inventory & Storage System
projects.tagline: Numbered asset codes, labeled storage and an equipment register for office and remote staff.

detail.problem: Equipment was untracked and scattered across desks and homes.
detail.solution: An asset inventory with numbered codes, labels, logs and a spreadsheet, plus labeled storage and a remote-equipment register.
highlights: Numbered asset codes in use from 2025
Agency-owned equipment register collected from remote staff (serial, brand, model)
Return-to-pool drive cleared unused equipment from desks (December 2025)
Labeled storage for monitors, headsets and spares; cube shelving installed (August 2026)

projects.name: shipping-station
projects.title: Shipping & Postage Station
projects.tagline: In-office shipping and USPS postage with a thermal label printer, scale and multi-carrier labels.

detail.problem: Packages and postage required trips out and manual label handling.
detail.solution: An in-office station for weighing, labeling and postage: Pitney Bowes labels and scale, USPS postage via Stamps.com, a Zebra ZD421 thermal printer and Shippo for multi-carrier labels.
highlights: Pitney Bowes shipping labels and scale set up (November 2025)
Zebra ZD421 thermal shipping printer added (April 2026)
Postal scale and USPS postage via Stamps.com; Shippo for multi-carrier labels
Postage charges reconciled against the card statement with no discrepancies

projects.name: ups-backup-rollout
projects.title: UPS Battery-Backup Rollout
projects.tagline: Battery backup for the office network, desks and every remote employee’s modem and router.

detail.problem: Power blips took down the office network and workstations, and remote staff lost connectivity during outages.
detail.solution: UPS coverage for office network gear and desks, and portable units for every remote employee’s modem and router.
highlights: Sourced exact replacement batteries for the office UPS fleet
Fire-code compliance research (NFPA 1 / Florida Fire Prevention Code, UL guidance) with five compliant installation options
Ordered portable UPS units for all remote staff plus spares at a volume discount (September 2026)

projects.name: supply-subscriptions
projects.title: Office Supply Management — Subscription Ordering
projects.tagline: Moved recurring office supplies from ad-hoc orders to managed subscriptions with a shared request queue.

detail.problem: Supplies were ordered ad hoc, one request at a time.
detail.solution: Recurring supplies on Amazon Business Subscribe & Save, with staff queuing requests in a shared cart instead of one-off orders.
highlights: Recurring drinks, snacks, coffee and paper on auto-order
Shared request cart replaces one-off orders
Account and ordering administered centrally

case_studies.title: Zap Watchdog
case_studies.summary: A three-layer monitoring program for Zapier automations (detection & routing → logging & accountability → routine maintenance) so silent Zap failures on revenue-critical voicemail routing get caught. Delivered as an SOP and a Zap Health Log workbook.

case_studies.title: reMarkable 2 rollout training
case_studies.summary: A 32-slide training deck verified against reMarkable software 3.27, an EOS Core Process document, and narrated videos with clickable in-video links (see koi-training-video-pipeline).

case_studies.title: Staff monthly quiz program
case_studies.summary: An evidence-based monthly quiz program (retrieval practice, spaced "Encore" re-testing, private scores, no leaderboards) with an Apps Script generator for the Google Forms (see koi-apps-script-toolkit).
